names_audience.instructions: Does the text say who it is for, by naming a kind of person, role or situation?

criteria.true: A reader can tell who is being addressed ("founders", "if you run payroll", "new runners").
criteria.false: It could be addressed to anyone.

concrete_detail.instructions: Does the text contain a specific number, name, time span or result?

criteria.true: It states a figure, a named thing or a measurable outcome.

opens_with_filler.instructions: Does the text open with a greeting, an introduction of the speaker, or a question that only names the topic?

criteria.true: It starts with "Hey guys", "In this video", "Welcome back", "Are you using X?" or similar.
criteria.false: It starts on the claim, the problem or the result.

unsupported_claim.instructions: Does the text use a guarantee or a superlative about itself: guaranteed, the best, the only, the first, number one, or a result promised to everyone?

criteria.true: It contains one of those claims.
criteria.false: It contains none of them. A specific result or figure on its own is not one.

one_idea.instructions: Does this slide make exactly one point?

criteria.true: One idea a reader could repeat in a sentence.
criteria.false: Two or more separate points, or no clear point.

clarity.instructions: How easy is the text to understand on one quick read by someone new to the subject?
criteria: Needs a second read to work out what is meant.
Clear on one read and could be repeated from memory.

hook_type.instructions: Which kind of opening is this?

criteria.bold_claim: States a strong or surprising claim.
criteria.mistake: Names a mistake the reader is making.
criteria.number: Leads with a figure or a counted list.
criteria.question: Asks a question the reader wants answered.
criteria.story: Starts a personal story or a specific moment.
